reforms.description: The federal government established the Canada Foundation for Innovation in February 1997 with C$800 million in funding over five years to modernise and enhance research infrastructure at post-secondary institutions and hospitals. The Foundation contributes approximately C$180 million annually to support infrastructure projects in partnership with private and voluntary sectors and provincial governments, funding modernisation of laboratories, computer networks, research databases, and related capital infrastructure in health, environment, science and engineering.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research infrastructure modernisation enhances research capacity and productivity, supporting long-term innovation and knowledge creation across multiple sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'created' and 'established' in 1997 Budget announcement; funding to be distributed over five years from 1997.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide investment in research infrastructure with substantial federal funding (C$800 million) and multi-sector partnership model represents a major reform to Canada's research capacity.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government introduced in the 1997 budget a proposal to create the Canada Foundation for Innovation. The main objectives of the Foundation will be to increase the country's ability to carry out world-class scientific research and technology development; to expand research and job opportunities for young Canadians; and to promote productive networks and collaboration among post-secondary educational institutions, research hospitals and the private sector.

reforms.description: Ontario's 1997 budget allocated C$500 million for a ten-year research and development fund to support innovation and research capacity in the province.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public R&D funding increases research capacity and knowledge creation, supporting long-term productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Announced in Ontario's 1997 budget; implementation timeline spans ten years from 1997.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant provincial R&D fund with substantial allocation (C$500 million over ten years) but narrower in scope than federal initiatives.
reforms.source_quote: C$ 500 million for a ten-year research and development fund

reforms.description: Canada introduced a refundable R&D tax credit for small firms and broadened the definition of R&D and technology for tax purposes as part of structural reform measures implemented between 1985 and 1996.
reforms.component_name: R&D tax credit for small firms
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Refundable R&D tax credits reduce the cost of R&D investment for small firms, incentivising private-sector innovation and improving allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states reforms were 'implemented between 1985–1996'; using first year per temporal assignment rules.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant structural reform to the tax treatment of R&D with broadened definitions, but implemented over an extended period (1985–1996) as part of a broader reform package.
reforms.source_quote: Introduced refundable R&D tax credit for small firms; broadened the definition of R&D and technology for tax purposes.

reforms.description: Canada created Networks of Centers of Excellence in 1988 to support collaborative research and knowledge transfer across institutions and sectors, fostering public-private research partnerships.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Collaborative research networks enhance knowledge transfer and institutional capacity, supporting innovation and productivity growth through improved knowledge diffusion.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'created in 1988', indicating established and operational programme.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant institutional innovation creating a new collaborative research infrastructure model, but narrower in scope and funding than the CFI.
reforms.source_quote: Created Networks of Centers of Excellence in 1988.

reforms.description: The federal government provided additional funding for the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) to stabilise its funding at C$97 million per year, encouraging research and innovation by small and medium-sized enterprises.
reforms.package_name: Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) Funding Stabilisation
reforms.component_name: Industrial Research Assistance Program funding stabilisation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Stable, dedicated funding for SME research assistance reduces barriers to R&D investment for smaller firms, supporting innovation and productivity growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'provided additional funding' and 'stabilise its funding at C$97 million per year', indicating active programme operation in 1997.
reforms.importance_rationale: Incremental adjustment to an existing programme (funding stabilisation) rather than a new instrument or structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: The recent Budget announced the renewal of the Networks of Centres of Excellence (NCE) programme with stable funding of C$47 million per year as well as additional funding for the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) to stabilise its funding at C$97 million per year. The IRAP programme encourages research and innovation by small and medium-sized enterprises.

reforms.description: Canada maintains tax credits available for research and development activities, supporting private-sector R&D investment through the tax system.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax credits reduce the effective cost of R&D investment, incentivising private-sector innovation and improving allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: Text uses present tense 'maintains', indicating ongoing operational status as of 1997 survey.
reforms.importance_rationale: Ongoing maintenance of an established tax instrument; no new reform or structural change indicated.
reforms.source_quote: substantial incentives exist for investing in R&D

reforms.description: Canada enhanced tax deductions for tuition and educational institution attendance, and increased contribution limits to Registered Education Savings Plans (RESPs) to defer tax on returns from post-secondary education savings.
reforms.component_name: Enhanced education tax deductions and RESP contribution limits
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax incentives for post-secondary education increase human capital accumulation, supporting long-term productivity and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text uses past tense 'enhanced' and 'increased', indicating reforms are in force as of 1997 survey.
reforms.importance_rationale: Incremental adjustment to education tax incentives; narrower in scope than major human capital reforms targeting research-specific talent pipelines.
reforms.source_quote: The tax treatment of human capital investment has been improved. Deductions for tuition and for students attending educational institutions have been enhanced, and contribution limits to Registered Education Savings Plans...have been increased.
